FINDING_ID: R1_RA_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `assign()` does not validate that `models` contains at least one distinct model after materialisation, nor that every element exposes the required attributes before scoring. This is broader than the prior duplicate-ID finding: because `models` is only checked for truthiness before `models_list = list(models)`, a one-shot iterator/generator can pass the `if not models` guard yet yield zero items. That leads `_compute_pool_max([])` to return zeros, `scores` to remain empty, and `pm_candidates[0]` to raise `IndexError` rather than a contract-level `ValueError`. This is a concrete API bug for any caller passing a consumed iterator or lazy iterable.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Materialise first, then validate: `models_list = list(models); if not models_list: raise ValueError(...)`. Also validate element shape early with explicit checks or a typed constructor boundary.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R1_RA_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: `assign()` and `reassign()` can emit role maps containing fewer entries than the number of distinct known models, with no explicit invariant or error, when `active_models` includes unknown IDs or omits known IDs. Prior reviewers noted silent skipping of unknown IDs in `reassign()`, but a separate issue remains: `reassign()` constructs `remaining_ids` from the caller-supplied set, then silently drops IDs not found in `models_for_scoring` during score computation (`if model is None: continue`). If all non-PM IDs are unknown, the method returns `{pm: PM}` even though `active_models` may claim a larger active pool. This creates an internally inconsistent state where role assignment no longer reflects the declared active set.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `active_models` exactly against the known model universe before reassignment. Raise on unknown IDs; optionally also require `active_models` to be a subset of known IDs and make omission semantics explicit. Add a postcondition check that every active known non-PM model receives a role.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R1_RA_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: `record_failure()` ignores its temporal contract and appends blindly to per-model history without using `round_idx` or any deduplication key, while `reassign(round_idx, ...)` claims to use failure history “for round r-1”. The effective penalty is therefore based on append count, not round alignment. Multiple failure recordings for the same model in one round, or missed recordings for another round, skew `phi_hist` permanently and silently. This is a semantic bug in the area’s own state model, independent of cross-component caller behavior.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Store failure history keyed by round index, e.g. `Dict[str, Dict[int, bool]]` or a fixed round-ordered structure. Make `record_failure(model_id, round_idx, failed)` overwrite per round rather than append. In `reassign()`, compute the intended aggregate explicitly (all prior rounds or a defined window).  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R1_RA_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: The documented score range in `_capability_score()` is unjustified and can be false: the docstring says the scalar capability score is in `[0, 1]`, but the implementation enforces no constraints on `config.get_alpha(role)` and does not bound or clip the dot product. Negative weights, weights summing to more than 1, or malformed normalized fingerprints can produce scores outside `[0,1]`. This matters because later logic and validators implicitly treat these as normalized comparables.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either enforce configuration invariants in `DynamicManagementConfig.__post_init__` (nonnegative weights summing to 1, normalized inputs in range) or remove the `[0,1]` claim and document the real admissible score domain. Add assertions/tests around score range if normalization is required by design.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R1_RA_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.57  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: `round_idx` in `reassign()` is dead state. It is accepted, documented as relevant to failure history, and then never used. This is not just cosmetic: it signals a mismatch between the advertised round-aware reassignment policy and the actual implementation, making it impossible to implement decay windows, previous-round-only hysteresis, or reproducible round-based audit semantics from this API.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either remove `round_idx` from the signature and docs if cumulative history is intended, or use it to index live state and failure history consistently. Prefer the latter because the API already exposes round semantics.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R1_RA_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.54  
DESCRIPTION: `assign()` does not validate that model IDs are non-empty strings or hash-stable identifiers suitable for use as durable keys across rounds. Prior findings covered uniqueness, but not identifier validity. Empty-string IDs, whitespace-only IDs, or IDs that differ only by caller-normalization conventions can be accepted and then propagated into `role_map`, `capability_scores`, failure history, and cross-component lookups. This undermines deterministic external integration and auditability.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `model_id` shape at assignment boundary: type `str`, non-empty after stripping, and optionally a canonical normalization rule. Reject invalid IDs before building any maps.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R1_RA_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.52  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47  
DESCRIPTION: `validate_k1()` and `validate_homogeneous()` are implemented as executable validators but can raise exceptions instead of returning `False` when the underlying constructors or score path fail. For example, `validate_homogeneous(0, config)` constructs an empty model list and then calls `assign()`, which raises `ValueError`; `validate_k1()` similarly assumes successful construction and indexing. As “validators”, these methods do not behave as total boolean predicates over their input domain.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Define and enforce input preconditions (`k >= 1`) or catch assignment exceptions and return `False`. Keep validators total and side-effect-free.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R1_RA_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.61  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION: `assign()`’s deterministic PM/COL tie-breaking is only deterministic relative to the incoming sequence order when both score and `_tie_break_key()` are equal. Because the final sort key omits a stable unique identifier such as `model_id`, exact-equality ties among distinct models collapse to Python sort stability on input order. Prior findings noted this for homogeneous validation and `reassign()` COL selection, but the same defect exists in initial PM and COL assignment itself whenever two models have identical fingerprints and equal scores. This weakens the stated “deterministic tie-breaking” contract.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Extend all ranking keys to include `model_id` (or another canonical unique key) as the final comparator. Example: `(score, tie_break_key, model_id)` with `reverse=True` adjusted carefully or use explicit tuple sign conventions.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R1_RA_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.44  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: Cross-component risk [unverified from this area alone]: `reassign()` accepts `live_fingerprints` as a partial overlay and silently mixes live and stale fingerprints in one scoring pass. If other components update only some models each round, role decisions compare heterogeneous time slices rather than a coherent snapshot. This can bias COL selection in favor of models whose stale estimates lag or lead reality. The issue is architectural because this area has no freshness metadata or snapshot consistency check.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Require `live_fingerprints` to be either complete for all active known models or tagged with a shared snapshot/version timestamp that `reassign()` validates. Otherwise reject partial mixed-epoch scoring or mark it explicitly as degraded mode.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: R1_RA_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.55  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.59  
DESCRIPTION: `get_ordering()` assumes every `capability_scores[mid]` contains every `role.value`, but this invariant is not protected after object construction because the dicts are mutable and publicly exposed. Even without malicious mutation, any future partial refresh logic can violate this shape and cause `KeyError`. This is distinct from the stale-score issue: the method depends on an unvalidated nested-dict schema at read time.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Encapsulate `capability_scores` behind immutable mappings or accessor methods, and validate/update the full schema atomically whenever scores change. At minimum, guard `get_ordering()` with explicit invariant checks and informative errors.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

Definitive stance: these are additional Role Assignment flaws not already captured in the prior findings list, with one explicitly marked cross-component and unverified from local scope.
